newsitem.title: BELGIUM: CLT-UFA TO CONTINUE FOREIGN EXPANSION - CEO.
newsitem.headline: CLT-UFA TO CONTINUE FOREIGN EXPANSION - CEO.

text.p: Luxembourg-based broadcaster CLT-UFA continues its expansion abroad in Poland, Sweden, the United Kingdom and Hungary, its chief executive officer Remy Sautter said on Monday.
Sautter told Belgian daily Le Soir that the group will launch its Polish-language RTL7 TV station in December.
RTL7 will be produced in Warsaw by a 50-strong team, made up 90 percent of Polish nationals, and will be broadcast via satellite from Luxembourg.
He said that a U.S. group might soon take a 50 percent stake in RTL7, which for now is a 100-pct CLT-UFA unit.

Sautter said that in Sweden the group was looking into applying for a broadcasting licence with the government or taking a stake in the capital of an existing television operation such as TV4 or Luxembourg-based Scandinavian Broadcasting System SA (SBS).

In the UK CLT-UFA has a 29 percent stake in Channel 5, the fifth terrestrial television channel, set to launch in March. "Channel 5 will be the last new major terrestrial television operation in Europe," he said.
In Hungary CLT-UFA is a candidate in the privatisation fo the second public channel, Sautter said.
In the UK, where CLT took a 49.9 percent stake in Talk Radio last year, the group is a candidate to take over FM frequencies which could be abandonned by current operators.

"The UK is the most promising market for private radio on Europe, because, until the start of the decade, there was no national private radio," he said. Radio advertising revenue in the UK was growing at a rate of 25 percent year.
Sautter hoped French pay-TV venture -- in which CLT-UFA has a 20 percent stake -- could be launched by Christmas.
Sautter is responsible for CLT-UFA's business outside Germany. Co-chief executive officer Rolf Schmidt-Holtz is responsible for Germany.

Asked about CLT-UFA's decision to ditch its plan for a digital pay television operation in Germany, Sautter said that the project was abandoned partly because of changes to the shareholdership level of the various partners involved.
Other reasons were the fact that the rival Kirch group had secured the rights to top U.S. movies before CLT-UFA and the fact that Germans were not that interested in pay TV to begin with.
"Germans are four times less interested than the French in paying for additional TV channels because they already have 30 channels," he said.

Sautter said the merger of Luxembourg broadcaster Compagnie Luxembourgeoise de Telediffusion SA (CLT) with the television interests of German publisher Bertelsmann (UFA) would be finalised in the first half of January.
Bertelsmann and CLT shareholder Audiofina signed the merger agreement in July. The European Union cleared the deal on October 7.
